Question: Can agents receive instructions, present results, and conduct HITL interactions within Teams and Copilot 365? Native or bridged?
Response: Native. Every human has a personal agent (PA) surfaced in M365 Copilot via M365 Agents SDK. The PA is grounded by Work IQ — the M365 work graph and memory layer — which gives it a rich, continuously-updated understanding of the human's role, expertise, collaboration patterns, calendar, and work velocity. This is what makes the PA personalised rather than a generic chat shell. It surfaces information proactively, recommends actions, drafts outputs, and triggers workflows on behalf of the human. Humans make all decisions — the PA prepares and executes. Example: Hiring Manager's PA surfaces a headcount gap in Teams (informed by Work IQ knowing the team's recent attrition and project pipeline), presents a draft requisition, and triggers the hiring workflow OBO the manager when approved. Finance BP's PA presents invoice approval requests with context and recommendation in Teams. All PA interactions feed back to the Control Plane — the HR BP's PA IS the Fleet Manager interface in Teams, while the full Control Plane UI provides the richer fleet management surface.
Key Technologies: M365 Agents SDK, GHCP SDK (PA agent), Work IQ (PA grounding), M365 Copilot
POC Demo: POC2: Show Hiring Manager receiving PA notification in Teams, reviewing draft requisition, and approving to kick off hiring workflow.

Question: Can agents monitor mailboxes, parse inbound email, extract intent, and compose/send responses; respecting DLP and email security policies?
Response: Yes. The human's PA handles email interaction via Microsoft Graph MCP server. The PA can: monitor the human's mailbox for relevant emails (invoice submissions, candidate communications), parse email content and extract intent/entities, compose contextual responses for the human's review. Outbound email is a non-revocable action — GHCP SDK hooks intercept the send, route to the human's PA for approval. After human approval, the email is sent deterministically (no LLM in the send path). DLP: Microsoft Purview DLP policies apply to all email interactions. Content safety: Foundry Guardrails check email content before composition. Finance BP receives approval requests via email Adaptive Cards with context, recommendation, and approve/reject buttons — response routes back through the PA to the Durable Functions orchestration.
Key Technologies: Microsoft Graph MCP, M365 Agents SDK, Purview DLP, GHCP SDK hooks (non-revocable action gate)
POC Demo: POC2: Show Finance BP receiving Adaptive Card approval request via email, approving, and workflow resuming automatically.

Question: Can agents expose and consume HTTP endpoints for event-driven triggering, status callbacks, and external integration?
Response: Yes. Azure Durable Functions natively exposes HTTP endpoints for: (1) Workflow triggering — external systems fire HTTP requests to start new workflows or raise events on waiting orchestrations. (2) Status queries — HTTP endpoint returns current workflow status, phase, and metadata. (3) Event callbacks — external systems notify the orchestration of completed actions (e.g. ServiceNow provisioning complete). MCP servers consume external APIs via HTTP. APIM AI Gateway provides managed API endpoints with auth, rate limiting, and monitoring. All webhook interactions are logged in OTEL telemetry and visible on the Control Plane.
Key Technologies: Azure Durable Functions HTTP endpoints, APIM AI Gateway, MCP servers
POC Demo: POC1: Show external system triggering invoice workflow via webhook, and callback notification when payment is processed.

Question: Do you support the A2A standard (Google/Linux Foundation): AgentCards, JSON-RPC task lifecycle, SSE streaming, gRPC? Can agents collaborate with off-platform agents on different stacks?
Response: Yes. A2A is natively supported via APIM AI Gateway. Agent card registration: each Hosted Agent publishes an AgentCard describing its capabilities, tools, and interaction protocols. APIM governs A2A interactions: JSON-RPC mediation, policy enforcement, auth, and audit logging. SSE streaming supported for long-running task status updates. Cross-platform collaboration: external agents on different stacks (Palantir, Salesforce, WPP Open) can interact with WPP's agents via A2A, governed by APIM policies. POC2 demonstrates A2A with an external candidate agent negotiating interview times — the candidate's external AI agent communicates via A2A with the Interview Coordinator skill, governed by APIM.
Key Technologies: APIM AI Gateway (A2A governance), AgentCards, JSON-RPC, SSE
POC Demo: POC2: Demonstrate A2A interop — external candidate agent negotiating interview times with the hiring workflow via A2A protocol.

Question: Can a single session engage multiple humans and multiple agents simultaneously with role-based visibility and capability-based routing; without serialisation bottlenecks?
Response: Yes. A single Durable Functions workflow orchestrates interactions with multiple humans across multiple surfaces concurrently. POC2 example: a single hiring workflow involves 5 humans (Hiring Manager in LA via Teams, HR BP in London via Control Plane, Finance BP in Mumbai via email, IT Ops in Chennai via ServiceNow, Candidate via web portal) — all interacting asynchronously. There is no serialisation bottleneck because: HITL waits are zero-compute external events on the Durable Functions orchestration, multiple wait_for_external_event calls can be active simultaneously, and each human's PA handles their interaction independently. Role-based visibility: each human sees only their relevant slice of the workflow via their preferred surface. Capability-based routing: Agent 365 determines which human receives which exception/approval based on role, authority, and availability. The Control Plane provides the unified cross-workflow view for fleet operators.
Key Technologies: Azure Durable Functions (parallel external events), M365 Agents SDK (PA per human), Agent 365 (routing), Entra RBAC
POC Demo: POC2: Show 5 humans across 4 timezones interacting with a single hiring workflow simultaneously via different surfaces.

Question: Can agents render rich interactive experiences: Adaptive Cards, forms, approval flows, data tables, charts, decision trees? Declaratively defined and dynamically composed at runtime?
Response: Yes. Adaptive Cards are the primary rich UI mechanism. The agentic loop composes Adaptive Cards dynamically based on workflow context — the card content, structure, and actions are determined by the skill at runtime. Supported in Teams, Outlook (email), and the Custom Control Plane UI. The Control Plane UI extends beyond Adaptive Cards with: data tables (workflow fleet view), charts (cost attribution, SLA tracking), decision trees (situational awareness drill-down), approval flows (bulk HITL with batch policies), and autonomy dials (threshold sliders). All UI components in the Control Plane are dynamically composed from Fleet Manager assessments and workflow state — not static screens. The Control Plane UI is a React application consuming real-time data via SignalR, Application Insights APIs, and Foundry REST APIs.
Key Technologies: Adaptive Cards, Custom Control Plane UI (React), SignalR (real-time), Fleet Manager dynamic composition
POC Demo: POC1: Show dynamically composed Adaptive Card for invoice approval in Outlook. Show Control Plane UI with data tables, charts, and bulk approval flow.
